messages.subject: Changing Dimnames to taxa names
parts:
Hi there, 

I'm relatively new to R and am wanting to utilize plotGMPhyloMorphoSpace. I've been able to build my tree and use it as class "phylo" but when using the above function I get:

Error in plotGMPhyloMorphoSpace(tree, mydata.gpa$coords, tip.labels = TRUE,  : 
  Number of taxa in data matrix and tree are not not equal.

I have a feeling it has something to do with the specimens dimnames as they are named by specimen and not taxa. I've tried a few different options to change the names to taxa but nothing seems to be working. Any tips would be greatly appreciated. Thanks so much, 

Joanna

messages.author: 4d71c6e24fb21497
messages.subject: RE: [geomorph-r-package] Changing Dimnames to taxa names
parts:
Joanna,

 

Yes, that is a common issue. Difficult to trouble-shoot without knowing what you have tried.  The best suggestion is for you to look at the help file for that function as well as its data. If you run the example then type

 

dimnames(Y.gpa$coords)

 

you will see how the species names are specified. So long as your data are in a 3D array like this one, and the names are in the 3rd dimension it will work.  Alternatively, if you have a 2D matrix and the rownames are the species names, it will also work.

 

Dean

messages.author: 4d71c6e24fb21497
messages.subject: RE: [geomorph-r-package] Re: Changing Dimnames to taxa names
parts:
Agh. You have the same names for multiple taxa. That will cause errors for all phylogeny-related R packages, as they don’t know which data point corresponds to which tip of the phylogeny.

 

You will need to make unique names in your dataset and your phylogeny, then have a 1-to-1 correspondence.

 

HINT: a good check for this is the function ‘treedata’ in geiger. It will match the tree and the data and prune them both to match. In looking at what is pruned out of the tree or the data matrix, you can find errors in your labels more easily.

Dean

messages.subject: Re: Changing Dimnames to taxa names

Dear Joanna,

Your data structure appears to be multiple specimens per species. In order to use the phylogenetic methods in geomorph and elsewhere, you have to first obtain species means. To do this, follow these instructions:
https://github.com/geomorphR/geomorph/wiki/Averaging-data-by-group

Emma
